end.summary: Named common non-metals and identified their states, including oxygen, nitrogen, chlorine, sulphur, iodine and graphite/carbon.
end.parentNote: Pari practised states of non-metals, their roles in living things, and uses such as graphite in pencils, chlorine in water, iodine in salt, nitrogen in chip packets and hydrogen as rocket fuel. They explained ideas using everyday examples and correctly described nitrogen as inert in sealed chip packets. There was an initial mix-up about carbon and helium in living things; it was corrected later by identifying carbon in the body, food and graphite (correctAfterLastSeen). At home, ask Pari to explain one non-metal use from an everyday object and name the relevant property.

Haan, khuli bhujia naram padne wala example bilkul fit hai. Hawa ki nami se crunch kam hota hai; oxygen tel ko kharab bhi kar sakti hai, aur packet mein nitrogen isse bachane mein madad karti hai. Ab ek alag non-metal dhoondhiye: pencil ki ‘lead’ asal mein kis non-metal ki bani hoti hai?
graphite hai na, maine toh pehle hi bataya tha ki pencils wala graphite carbon se banta hai, lead toh sirf naam hai, asal mein carbon hota hai

Haan, aapne graphite ko carbon se joda tha; pencil ki ‘lead’ carbon ka hi ek roop hai. Ab rocket wala ulta example sochiye: liquid hydrogen oxygen ke saath jalta hai. Exhaust mein kya niklega, aur hydrogen accha fuel kyon hai?

hydrogen aur oxygen jaale toh pani banega na, H2O. exhaust mein steam niklegi, jaise kettle mein se. aur hydrogen accha fuel hai kyunki yeh light hai aur bohat energy deta hai, rocket ko upar bhejne ke liye

Aapne paani ki bhaap aur hydrogen se milne wali energy ki baat ki. Hydrogen oxygen ke saath jalne par water vapour banata hai; rocket mein yeh reaction bahut energy deti hai. Chips ke packet mein nitrogen fuel ki tarah kyun nahi jalti?
